desc:
Count the contiguous non-empty subarrays of nums whose product is strictly positive. Subarrays at different positions count separately even if their values are equal.

Example: for [1, -2, -3, 4] the positive-product subarrays are [1], [4], [-2, -3], [1, -2, -3], [-2, -3, 4] and the whole array, so the answer is 6.
hints: Only the signs matter, and a zero cuts the array into independent segments.
For subarrays ending at index i, count how many have a positive product and how many a negative one. Add the positive count to the answer at every index.
Positive x: pos += 1, neg unchanged. Negative x: new pos = neg, new neg = pos + 1. Zero: both become 0.
editorial: Let pos and neg count the subarrays ending at the current index with a positive / negative product. Appending a positive number keeps every sign and adds the one-element subarray [x] to the positive group. Appending a negative number flips every sign (so the two counts swap) and the single-element subarray [x] joins the negative group. A zero makes every subarray ending there have product 0, so both counts reset.
Add pos to the running total at each index. The answer can reach about 5 × 107, still inside 32 bits. O(n) time, O(1) space.
